citations.excerpt: Dampness of habitable rooms.
Visible mold growth, as determined by a health officer or a code enforcement officer
until the lessor has notice of the dilapidation or if the tenant is in violation of Section 1941.2.

hazard_laws.landlord_duty: Dampness that endangers occupants can make a unit substandard. Mold only counts as substandard once a health or code enforcement officer determines it. The landlord's mold repair duty starts when they have notice.
tenant_options: Give the landlord written notice and keep proof of when and how
Document with dated photos
Ask your city or county code enforcement (or environmental health) office for an inspection
Talk to free legal aid before using any rent remedy
hazard_laws.deadline_note: No fixed repair deadline in these sections.
cautions: A photo or AI label is never an officer's determination
Minor mold on surfaces meant to get wet (like a shower) is excluded
Do not presume the tenant caused it

citations.excerpt: Effective waterproofing and weather protection of roof and exterior walls, including unbroken windows and doors.
Deteriorated or ineffective waterproofing of exterior walls, roofs, foundations, or floors, including broken windows or doors.
All plumbing, except plumbing that conformed with all applicable laws in effect at the time of installation and has been maintained in good condition

hazard_laws.landlord_duty: A unit that substantially lacks effective waterproofing and weather protection is untenantable. Leaking roofs, walls or windows and badly maintained plumbing can make a building substandard.
tenant_options: Give the landlord written notice and keep proof of when and how
Document with dated photos of the leak and any damage
Ask your city or county code enforcement (or environmental health) office for an inspection
Talk to free legal aid before using any rent remedy
hazard_laws.deadline_note: No fixed repair deadline in these sections.
cautions: Whether a leak is substantial enough is a judgment for an inspector or court
Do not presume the tenant caused it

citations.excerpt: kept in every part clean, sanitary, and free from all accumulations of debris, filth, rubbish, garbage, rodents, and vermin.
Infestation of insects, vermin, or rodents as determined by a health officer

hazard_laws.landlord_duty: Areas under the landlord's control must be kept free of rodents and vermin. An infestation makes a building substandard once a health officer (or, where there is no health officer agreement, a code enforcement officer) determines it.
tenant_options: Give the landlord written notice and keep proof of when and how
Document with dated photos of droppings, nests or damage
Ask your city or county code enforcement (or environmental health) office for an inspection
Talk to free legal aid before using any rent remedy
hazard_laws.deadline_note: No fixed repair deadline in these sections.
cautions: Signs in a photo are not an officer's determination of infestation
Do not presume the tenant caused it

citations.excerpt: Electrical lighting, with wiring and electrical equipment that conformed with applicable law at the time of installation, maintained in good working order.
All wiring, except that which conformed with all applicable laws in effect at the time of installation if it is currently in good and safe condition and working properly.

hazard_laws.landlord_duty: Wiring and electrical equipment must be maintained in good working order. Wiring that is not in good and safe condition can make a building substandard.
tenant_options: Keep away from exposed wiring and do not try to fix it yourself
Give the landlord written notice and keep proof of when and how
Document with dated photos from a safe distance
Ask your city or county code enforcement (or environmental health) office for an inspection
Talk to free legal aid before using any rent remedy
hazard_laws.deadline_note: No fixed repair deadline in these sections.
cautions: For sparks, burning smell or shocks, call 911 or the fire department first
Whether wiring is unsafe is for an inspector to decide

citations.excerpt: is deemed to be in violation of this part as to any portion that contains lead hazards.
“lead hazards” means deteriorated lead-based paint, lead-contaminated dust, lead-contaminated soil, or disturbing lead-based paint without containment

hazard_laws.landlord_duty: A building is in violation of state housing law where it contains lead hazards, such as deteriorated lead-based paint or lead-contaminated dust, at or above the state regulatory levels.
tenant_options: Give the landlord written notice and keep proof of when and how
Document with dated photos of peeling or chipping paint
Ask your city or county code enforcement (or environmental health) office for an inspection

Talk to free legal aid before using any rent remedy
hazard_laws.deadline_note: No fixed repair deadline in this section.
cautions: Peeling paint is not proof of lead; only testing against the Title 17 levels shows a lead hazard
Do not sand or scrape the paint

Lack of adequate heating.

hazard_laws.landlord_duty: Heating facilities must be maintained in good working order. Lack of adequate heating can make a building substandard.
tenant_options: Give the landlord written notice and keep proof of when and how
Keep a dated log of indoor temperatures
Ask your city or county code enforcement (or environmental health) office for an inspection
Talk to free legal aid before using any rent remedy

cautions: State law here sets no minimum temperature; local codes may

citations.excerpt: shall install a carbon monoxide device, approved and listed by the State Fire Marshal pursuant to Section 13263, in each existing dwelling unit having a fossil fuel burning heater or appliance, fireplace, or an attached garage
shall maintain carbon monoxide devices in that dwelling unit
The carbon monoxide device shall be operable at the time that the tenant takes possession.

hazard_laws.landlord_duty: Units with a fossil fuel heater or appliance, fireplace or attached garage need a carbon monoxide device. A landlord must keep it working, have it operable at move-in, and fix it once told it is broken or missing.
tenant_options: If a carbon monoxide alarm sounds or anyone feels dizzy or sick, get outside and call 911
Tell the landlord in writing that the device is missing or not working
Ask your city or county code enforcement (or environmental health) office for an inspection
Talk to free legal aid before using any rent remedy
hazard_laws.deadline_note: The landlord is not in violation for a broken device until notified.
cautions: The tenant has to tell the landlord about a broken or missing device

general_rules.summary: General duty to repair conditions that make a unit untenantable.
Lists what a unit must have to be tenantable, and counts any unit that is substandard under Health and Safety Code 17920.3 or 17920.10 as untenantable.

Repair-and-deduct or move out, only after notice and landlord neglect. Capped at one month's rent, no more than twice in 12 months. 30 days after notice is presumed reasonable, but it is not a universal deadline.

In an eviction case, a presumption that the landlord breached habitability can arise if an officer gave written notice after inspection and the conditions stayed unfixed 60 days later without good cause.

Limits on collecting rent only when an official inspection found the problem, an officer gave written notice, and it stayed unfixed 35 days after that official notice. The 35 days run from the officer's notice, not the tenant's letter.
Protection against retaliation for up to 180 days after a repair request, complaint or inspection, with conditions. Not blanket protection from eviction.
After 12 months of lawful occupancy, many tenancies can only be ended for a just cause stated in the notice. Many units are exempt.

city_procedures.name: Local code enforcement inspection
city_procedures.how: Cities, and counties for unincorporated areas, inspect rental housing on complaint. A written notice from an inspector is what Civil Code 1942.3 and 1942.4 rely on. Search your city or county name plus "code enforcement" to find the office.
